chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: Guy Kelly playing like Louis Armstrong at the Fairgrounds
summary: Guy Kelly sounded exactly like Armstrong and held a thousand people quiet; Milt recalls his handkerchief for his bumpy face.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: And Guy Kelly had started playing Louis Armstrong's thing. 'Everybody Loves Ma Baby' -- he played that on the trumpet. And he played 'What Did I Do To Be So Black and Blue?' [SINGS REFRAIN] And he was playing, and just like it was so easy... And he had a straw hat, and it was pulled down all around him. And he was an outstanding figure. He played so masterfully. See, these other guys, they played with the trumpet on the side of their lip or they looked like they were searching for something. Not Guy.
Everything he played was perfection. Not Louis Armstrong, but this was a man that sounded just like him. The image of Armstrong. Fantastic!
And the people were spellbound at the Fairgrounds. There was about a thousand people just standing around. And when you get a thousand Negroes to stay quiet, you have accomplished something.
Ain't nobody movin', ain't nobody sayin' nothin'. They're just looking. A thousand, just sitting there, just compact(?), quiet out there. Gee whiz, if you want a peace (?), it's Guy Kelly!
He even used a handkerchief, too! Because his face was very bumpy, so he used to wipe his face.

Yeah, he had this big bump that would come up on his face, white bumps when he would blow, and they would break, and he always kept a handkerchief. He was very sensitive to it, because he was a very neat man...
Shoes. Didn't he have pretty shoes?
